gate: You hold the lantern steady while the choir of the sunk sings your name back to you.
A drowned face rises under the ice and you do not look away until it sinks.
The dark asks for the lantern and you refuse it, though the wick is nearly gone.
You bargain with the bell keeper for passage and give him a name you no longer use.
Something breathes behind the ossuary door and you keep your feet on the wet stone.
You witness the drowned watchman rise from his chair and you do not step back.
A voice in the cistern offers you the way out for your shadow and you refuse.
You defy the chain that hums at your throat and walk on through the humming hall.
The rust whispers that the others have left you and you resist the urge to run.
You bargain with the thing under the ferry for a crossing and it asks for your voice.
You witness the choir of the sunk open their eyes and you keep counting the steps.
The lantern gutters to a blue bead and you sit in the black until it climbs again.
A hand of green bone closes on your ankle and you refuse to cry out in the flooded hall.
The drowned bell says lie down and you climb the salt stair instead.
The salt on the wall spells your mother's name and you walk past it without a word.
You resist the sleep the cold offers as the water reaches your chest.
You bargain with the keeper of the chains for a key and give up the hour of your birth.
You witness the sunk ship turn over in the black and you do not lose count of the rope.
A door of ribs asks for your true name before it opens and you give it silence.
You stand in the drowned chapel while the water sings and you do not add your voice.
chain: You hold your breath as the choir passes, then hold your nerve when it stops beside you.
You refuse the cistern voice once, and when it wears a friend's face you refuse again.
You bargain with the ferryman for passage, then keep your word when the far bank moves.
You witness the drowned rise from their pews, then walk the aisle between them.
You resist the cold's soft bargain at the knees, then resist it again at the throat.
You defy the bell that says kneel, then defy the chain that reaches out to make you.
You sit with the dying lantern through the black, and when it wakes you are still there.
You give the door of ribs your name, then stand while it says it back in a drowned voice.
